fact: The Tanzania Revenue Authority launched the Zanzibar Single Window System at a ceremony on 2 June 2026, a digital platform for customs clearance bringing various government agencies under one electronic gateway.
The article says the Tanzania Electronic Single Window System has already been established on Mainland Tanzania to connect traders, customs authorities and regulatory agencies.

The World Customs Organization says the Tanzania Revenue Authority and Zambia Revenue Authority held a bilateral workshop on 2-6 September 2024 to integrate their automated Customs systems for electronic exchange of Customs data.

The Tanzania Revenue Authority's delegation head says Tansis is the software used in Tanzania for declaring and clearing goods, with its data shared directly to the TECTS and RECTS cargo tracking systems.

Daily News reports Tanzania Ports Authority's director of ICT saying the Tanzania Revenue Authority rolled out a new version of its customs system TANCIS in early 2025, with clearance requests filed online.
Daily News reports the Tanzania Ports Authority saying the port and TRA systems are fully connected through the TANESW single window, which links TRA, TBS, TMDA and GCLA on one platform.

TradeMark Africa reports that the customs systems of Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi are interconnected through the East African Community Single Customs Territory Centralised Platform, with Tanzania's ports authority also connected.
